answer: A strong sybil defense is to let trust rise like dawn over a ridge, gradually and visibly, not all at once. An island is not settled by arriving in a fleet overnight; it is occupied slowly, with shelters built, paths marked, and neighbours learning who can be relied on. Likewise, an agent economy can give new identities almost no weight at first, then increase their standing only as they complete small, checkable tasks that peers attest. A swarm of fresh accounts may look impressive at first light, but without a long trail of verified work, its influence should stay near zero.
